properties.foundation_analysis: Subterranean foundation situated on the Carboniferous sedimentary strata of the Midland Valley Basin, composed of interbedded Sandstone, Siltstone, and Mudstone of the Gullane Formation overlain by dense glacial till (boulder clay). Primary historic load-bearing lithics derive from local Upper Carboniferous blond/grey sandstone quarries, predominantly fine-to-medium grained quartz arenite from the Craigleith and Hailes quarries. Structural mortar consists of historic non-hydraulic to feebly hydraulic hot-mixed lime and aggregate blends, with localized modern Portland cement repointing across secondary rear elevations. Groundwater hydrology follows the natural northward descending glacial slope toward the Firth of Forth.

properties.primary_surfacing: Engineered roadway and paved pedestrian curbs
properties.wear_characteristics: Authentic environmental patina and drainage grading

properties.botanical_analysis: Rear tenement gardens and Broughton Street Lane boundaries support mature urban deciduous flora dominated by *Acer pseudoplatanus* (Sycamore) and *Betula pendula* (Silver Birch). Late-August phenological expression exhibits dense, fully expanded dark green foliage with early localized chlorotic margins, firm branch architecture, and zero premature defoliation.

properties.architectural_summary: Classic Edinburgh New Town eastern periphery vernacular spanning late 18th to mid-19th-century Georgian and early Victorian tenement typologies alongside lower-scale rear mews and light-industrial infill. Broughton Street main elevations exhibit 3-to-4 storey plus basement and mansard attic massing, rectified to true vertical load-bearing planes. Roofscape features complex intersections of double-pitch gables, Scottish slate roofs with zinc/lead ridge capping, pitched timber-framed clerestories, pitched profile metal warehouse roofs, and flat felt/bitumen membranes. Rear elevations present irregular coursed sandstone masonry with projecting stone chimney stacks, clay chimney pots (cans), and regular vertical fenestration bays fitted with traditional timber-framed 6-over-6 and 2-over-2 sash-and-case windows.
